```{r Package Imports, message = F, warning = F}
# Warnings and startup messages suppressed
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggpmisc)
library(here)
library(gsw)
library(R.matlab)
library(ggbreak)
library(reshape2) # To make the ASV table into something that can be combined with environmental data
library(stringr)
```

# Import data 

```{r}
Sp_ASV_18Sv4 <- read_csv(here("Manuscript_Plots", "OCNMS_final_data", "18Sv4", "Decontam_final_taxonomy_table_pr2.csv")) # 18Sv4 data cleanedd by Sam
envData_BIG <- read_csv(here("Manuscript_Plots", "OCNMS_final_data", "18Sv4", "Decontam_final_metadata.csv")) %>% # metadata cleaned by Sam
  mutate(year = as.factor(year(eventDate))) %>%
    relocate(year, .after = eventDate)
envData <- envData_BIG %>%
  select(samp_name, pcr_plate_id, filename, eventDate, year, input_read_count, output_read_count, decimalLongitude, station_id, decimalLatitude, verbatimLongitude, verbatimLatitude, verbatimCoordinateSystem, geo_loc_name, verbatimEventDate, samp_collect_device, samp_size, samp_size_unit, minimumDepthInMeters, maximumDepthInMeters, DepthInMeters_method, tot_depth_water_col, temp, salinity, diss_oxygen, diss_oxygen_unit, replicate_number, expedition_id, measurements_from, region)
ASV_table <- read_csv(here("Manuscript_Plots", "OCNMS_final_data", "18Sv4", "Decontam_final_asv_table.csv"))
```


# Transpose & Join the data

Goal: 

| sample name | lat | lon | species | detected t/f | 
|-------------|-----|-----|---------|--------------|
| s1          | 1.  | 2.  | fish.   | T            |

```{r Data join}
# The metadata is associated with samples so I think it doesn't need rounding

# I need to combine observations with environmental data
# ASV_table has sample names as columns
# Reads_Species identifies sequences as species

Rds_Txa_18Sv4_pre <- full_join(Sp_ASV_18Sv4, ASV_table)

transpose_test <- Rds_Txa_18Sv4_pre[1:5,]

transposed_test <- melt(transpose_test, id.vars = c("seq_id", "iter", "ASV", "Taxon", "Confidence"), variable.name = "Sample", value.name = "Reads")

# okay, that came out right, here we go. pray for my RAM or whatever.

Rds_Txa_18Sv4 <- melt(Rds_Txa_18Sv4_pre, id.vars = c("seq_id", "iter", "ASV", "Taxon", "Confidence"), variable.name = "Sample", value.name = "Reads")
system("say Transpose complete")

eDNAxEnvData <- full_join(Rds_Txa_18Sv4, envData, by = join_by(Sample == samp_name))
system("say Data Join 1 complete")
```

# Filter & Export the combined data

```{r}
# Take a looksee to see which dissolved things are actually collected
# Basically only oxygen, the other columns are just for standardization
# View(eDNAxEnvData[110:150])
# Select the columns I care more about, and add a Taxon column with only the most specific taxon. Also, remove unassigned taxa, I don't care because I'm not doing eDNA index right now. Note to self, re-add unassigned taxa if doing eDNA index for total reads situation
smaller <- eDNAxEnvData %>% select(Taxon, iter, Reads, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude, eventDate, year, temp, salinity, expedition_id, diss_oxygen, diss_oxygen_unit) %>%
  filter(Taxon != "Unassigned") %>%
  filter(Taxon != "Eukaryota") %>%
  mutate(Lowest_taxon = str_split_i(string = Taxon, pattern = ';', i = -1)) %>%
  relocate(Lowest_taxon, .before = iter) %>%
  relocate(Taxon, .after = diss_oxygen_unit)

system("say Data Join 2 Complete")

# Export the joined data
write_csv(eDNAxEnvData, here("Manuscript_Plots", "OCNMS_final_Data", "18Sv4_eDNAxEnvData.csv"))
```

# Sampling Window Plots

```{r}
md <- envData

unique(md$expedition_id)

unique(md$samp_collect_method)

md_pps <- md %>% 
  filter(samp_collect_device == "McLane Particle and Phytoplankton Sampler")

sampledatelist <- with_tz(as.POSIXct(md_pps$eventDate, 
                             tz = "America/Los_Angeles",
                             tryFormats = c("%m/%d/%Y")))
sampledatelist <- as.data.frame(sampledatelist) %>%
  mutate(year = year(sampledatelist)) # this is necessary for faceting + individual sample plotting to work together

md_ctd <- md %>% # This is actually the metadata for CTD and the other type of bottle we used when the CTD was broken
  filter(samp_collect_device != "McLane Particle and Phytoplankton Sampler")

ctddatelist <- with_tz(as.POSIXct(md_ctd$eventDate, 
                             tz = "America/Los_Angeles",
                             tryFormats = c("%m/%d/%Y")))
ctddatelist <- as.data.frame(ctddatelist) %>%
  mutate(year = year(ctddatelist))
```

## Aesthetics (vars)
```{r}
widthpx <- 4000 # Width for export (pixels)
heightpx <- 2000 # Height for export (pixels)

widthpx_stacked <- 2000 # Width for export (pixels) for the stacked plots
heightpx_stacked <- 2000 # Height for export (pixels) for the stacked plots

# Rectangle windows aesthetics
width = 1
linecolor = "black"
fillcolor = "navy"

# CTD line or dot aesthetics
ctdcolor = "firebrick4"
# Add CTD as either point or line - uncomment whatever one you want
CTD_add <- geom_point(inherit.aes = F, data = ctddatelist, aes(x = ctddatelist, y = 0), color = ctdcolor)
#CTD_add <- geom_vline(inherit.aes = F, data = ctddatelist, aes(xintercept = ctddatelist), color = ctdcolor)
# Inherit_aes needs to be false, otherwise the main data will override it and cause an error

# Adding text labels
labely <- 0
labelsize <- 3
```

```{r}
# Find start and end dates for expeditions
stend <- envData %>% 
  select(eventDate, expedition_id) %>% 
  filter(year(eventDate) != 2019) %>% # it's two days and doesn't even graph.
  group_by(expedition_id) %>% 
  summarize(start = min(eventDate), end = max(eventDate)) %>%
  mutate(year = year(start),
         x_min = case_when(year == 2021 ~ as.POSIXct("2021-05-01"),
                          year == 2022 ~ as.POSIXct("2022-05-01"),
                          year == 2023 ~ as.POSIXct("2023-05-01")),
         x_max = case_when(year == 2021 ~ as.POSIXct("2021-11-01"),
                          year == 2022 ~ as.POSIXct("2022-11-01"),
                          year == 2023 ~ as.POSIXct("2023-11-01"))) # adds something to graph blank to force full field season to show in facet_wrap 
#scale_x_break(as.POSIXct(c("2021-11-01", "2022-05-01"))) +
  #scale_x_break(as.POSIXct(c("2022-11-01", "2023-05-01"))) 
stend
stend_t <- as.data.frame(t(stend %>% select(start,end)))
stend_t
```

## Sampling Window Graph 1
```{r}
# Graph 1: All in one graph

winplot <- ggplot(data = stend, 
       mapping = aes(x = start, y = 0, xend = end, yend = 0)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12), 
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"), # facet label background
        axis.text.x.top = element_blank(), # Needed to delete the extra axis created by ggbreak
        axis.ticks.x.top = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x.top = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "white")) +
  geom_segment(size = 200, 
       colour = fillcolor,
       alpha = 0.2) +
  # scale break is breaking coord_cartesian(lim) https://github.com/YuLab-SMU/ggbreak/issues/59 put cartesian before
  scale_x_datetime(breaks = "month", date_labels = "%b-%y", limits = as.POSIXct(c("2021-05-01", "2023-11-01"))) +
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, 0.5)) + # Zooms in the plot without deleting rectangle
  ylim(c(-0.01, 0.01)) +
  # clip = "off" allows data points to be drawn in the margins
  # expand = 0 doesn't add an expansion factor to the limits to keep the data off the axes
  ggtitle("PPS Deployment Windows") +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("") +
  scale_x_break(as.POSIXct(c("2021-11-01", "2022-05-01"))) +
  scale_x_break(as.POSIXct(c("2022-11-01", "2023-05-01"))) 

ggsave(plot = winplot,
       filename = here("Manuscript_Plots/Deployment_Window/DeploymentWindowsBoxesSimple.png"), 
           width = widthpx, 
           height = heightpx, 
           units = "px")
```



## Stacked Years

```{r}
# Graph 2: Stacked Years
# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42588238/setting-individual-y-axis-limits-with-facet-wrap-not-with-scales-free-y
winplot_stk <- ggplot(data = stend, 
       mapping = aes(x = start, y = 0, xend = end, yend = 0)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12), 
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"), # facet label background
        axis.text.x.top = element_blank(), # Needed to delete the extra axis created by ggbreak
        axis.ticks.x.top = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x.top = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "white")) +
  geom_segment(size = 200, # main plot
       colour = fillcolor,
       alpha = 0.2) +
    # scale break is breaking coord_cartesian(lim)     https://github.com/YuLab-SMU/ggbreak/issues/59 put cartesian before
  scale_x_datetime(breaks = "month", date_labels = "%b-%y") + #, limits = as.POSIXct(c("2021-05-01", "2023-11-01"
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, 0.5)) + # Zooms in the plot without deleting rectangle
  ylim(c(-0.01, 0.01)) +
  geom_blank(aes(x = x_min)) + # Adds the x_min column to force the x-axis to include the whole field season - it's just some invisible stuff in May and November to make the stacked plot look nice
  geom_blank(aes(x = x_max)) + 
  facet_wrap(vars(year), scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  # clip = "off" allows data points to be drawn in the margins
  # expand = 0 doesn't add an expansion factor to the limits to keep the data off the axes
  ggtitle("PPS Deployment Windows") +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("") 

winplot_stk

ggsave(plot = winplot_stk,
       filename = here("Manuscript_Plots/Deployment_Window/DeploymentWindowsBoxesStacked.png"), 
           width = widthpx_stacked, 
           height = heightpx_stacked, 
           units = "px")
```

## Each Sample Marked

```{r}
# Graph 3: Each sample marked
winplt_mrk <- ggplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12), 
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"), # facet label background
        axis.text.x.top = element_blank(), # Needed to delete the extra axis created by ggbreak
        axis.ticks.x.top = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x.top = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "white")) +
  geom_segment(data = stend, # data is down here now to avoid conflicts with geom_vline
       mapping = aes(x = start, y = 0, xend = end, yend = 0),
       size = 200, 
       colour = fillcolor,
       alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(inherit.aes = F, 
             data = sampledatelist,
             mapping = aes(xintercept = sampledatelist), 
             color = "black") + # add each individual sample
  # scale break is breaking coord_cartesian(lim) https://github.com/YuLab-SMU/ggbreak/issues/59 put cartesian before
  scale_x_datetime(breaks = "month", date_labels = "%b-%y", limits = as.POSIXct(c("2021-05-01", "2023-11-01"))) +
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, 0.5)) + # Zooms in the plot without deleting rectangle
  ylim(c(-0.01, 0.01)) +
  # clip = "off" allows data points to be drawn in the margins
  # expand = 0 doesn't add an expansion factor to the limits to keep the data off the axes
  ggtitle("PPS Deployment Windows") +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("") +
  scale_x_break(as.POSIXct(c("2021-11-01", "2022-05-01"))) +
  scale_x_break(as.POSIXct(c("2022-11-01", "2023-05-01"))) 

winplt_mrk

ggsave(plot = winplt_mrk,
       filename = here("Manuscript_Plots/Deployment_Window/DeploymentWindowsBoxesLines.png"), 
           width = widthpx, 
           height = heightpx, 
           units = "px")
```

## Add model data
```{r}
eDNAxEnvDataJoin1 <- eDNAxEnvData %>%
  mutate(source = "Mooring", temp = as.numeric(temp), diss_oxygen = as.numeric(diss_oxygen)) # missing has been converted to NA

model_37m <- read_csv(here("Manuscript_Plots", "LiveOcean_TH042_2021_2023_DepthClean_2.csv")) %>% 
  mutate(DateMatch = Date_UTC) %>% # name the column the same for the join to work
  mutate(source = "Model") # this has every hour on the hour

eDNAxEnvDataJoin <- eDNAxEnvDataJoin1 %>%
  mutate(DateMatch = round_date(eventDate, unit = "hour")) # need to round to the nearest hour to be able to join with model_37m

eDNAxEnv_Model1 <- left_join(eDNAxEnvDataJoin, model_37m, by = join_by(DateMatch))

eDNAxEnv_Model1 %>%
  group_by(DateMatch) %>%
  summarize(TEMP = mean(temp), O2 = mean(diss_oxygen))

pers_pwobwems <- eDNAxEnv_Model1 %>%
  filter(is.na(temp) | is.na(diss_oxygen)) %>%
  group_by(DateMatch) %>%
  summarize(TEMP = mean(temp), O2 = mean(diss_oxygen))

pwob_dates <- pers_pwobwems$DateMatch
model_37m %>% filter(DateMatch %in% pwob_dates)
eDNAxEnvDataJoin %>% filter(DateMatch %in% pwob_dates)

# I think I just need to create new columns?
```

```{r}
# lowercase is from the metadata, Temp_C and Oxygen_mg_L are from the model
eDNAxEnv_Model <- eDNAxEnv_Model1 %>%
  mutate(temp_comb = case_when(is.na(temp) ~ Temp_C, .default = temp),
         DO_comb = case_when(is.na(diss_oxygen) ~ Oxygen_mg_L, .default = diss_oxygen),
         temp_source = case_when(is.na(temp) ~ "Model", .default = "Mooring"),
         DO_source = case_when(is.na(diss_oxygen) ~ "Model", .default = "Mooring"))

Pwoblems2 <- eDNAxEnv_Model %>%
  filter(is.na(temp_comb) | is.na(DO_comb))
Pwoblems2 %>%
  group_by(expedition_id) %>%
  summarize(N = n())
Pwoblems2 %>%
  group_by(DateMatch) %>%
  summarize(N = n())

check <- eDNAxEnv_Model %>% select(DateMatch, temp, Temp_C, temp_comb, temp_source, diss_oxygen, Oxygen_mg_L, DO_comb, DO_source) # Spot check looks correct, there are no longer empty spaces!
```

# Export the joined, cleaned, and model-included data

```{r}
eDNAxEnv_Model_sp <- eDNAxEnv_Model %>%
  mutate(Lowest_Taxon = sub('.+;(.+)', '\\1', Taxon))

eDNAxEnv_Model_sp %>% select(Taxon, Lowest_Taxon)
```


```{r}
eDNAxEnv_Model_export <- eDNAxEnv_Model_sp %>%
  mutate(Temp_Celsius = temp_comb, DO_mg_L = DO_comb) %>%
  select(Lowest_Taxon, Sample, Reads, eventDate, DateMatch, year, 
         station_id, samp_collect_device,
         Temp_Celsius, DO_mg_L, temp_source, DO_source,
         seq_id, iter, ASV, Taxon, Confidence, pcr_plate_id, filename, 
         input_read_count, output_read_count, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude,
         verbatimLongitude, verbatimLatitude, verbatimCoordinateSystem, 
         geo_loc_name, verbatimEventDate, samp_size, samp_size_unit,
         minimumDepthInMeters, maximumDepthInMeters, DepthInMeters_method,
         tot_depth_water_col, replicate_number, expedition_id, measurements_from, region, Date_UTC, Depth) 

eDNAxEnv_Model_small <- eDNAxEnv_Model_sp %>%
  mutate(Temp_Celsius = temp_comb, DO_mg_L = DO_comb) %>%
  select(Lowest_Taxon, Sample, Reads, eventDate, DateMatch, year, 
         station_id, samp_collect_device,
         Temp_Celsius, DO_mg_L, temp_source, DO_source,
         iter, Taxon, decimalLongitude,
         decimalLatitude, replicate_number, expedition_id, Depth)

# Group by lowest taxon, add up across ASVs
eDNAxEnv_Model_small <- eDNAxEnv_Model_sp %>%
  mutate(Temp_Celsius = temp_comb, DO_mg_L = DO_comb) %>%
  group_by(eventDate, Lowest_Taxon, 
           replicate_number, samp_collect_device) %>%
  summarize(totReads = sum(Reads), 
            Sample = paste(unique(Sample), collapse = ', '), 
            DateMatch = paste(unique(DateMatch), collapse = ', '), 
            year = paste(unique(year), collapse = ', '), 
            station_id = paste(unique(station_id), collapse = ', '), 
            Temp_Celsius = mean(Temp_Celsius), 
            DO_mg_L = mean(DO_mg_L), 
            temp_source = paste(unique(temp_source), collapse = ', '), 
            DO_source = paste(unique(DO_source), collapse = ', '),
            iter = paste(unique(iter), collapse = ', '), 
            Taxon = paste(unique(Taxon), collapse = ', '), 
            decimalLongitude = paste(unique(decimalLongitude), collapse = ', '),
            decimalLatitude = paste(unique(decimalLatitude), collapse = ', '), 
            expedition_id = paste(unique(expedition_id), collapse = ', '), 
            Depth = paste(unique(Depth), collapse = ', '))
```


```{r}
# Export the joined data
write_csv(eDNAxEnv_Model_export, here("Manuscript_Plots", "OCNMS_final_Data", "18Sv4_eDNAxEnvData_Full.csv"))
write_csv(eDNAxEnv_Model_small, here("Manuscript_Plots", "OCNMS_final_Data", "18Sv4_eDNAxEnvData_Full_small.csv"))
```
